chunks: And ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān narrated from him:
Regarding a man who departed from Jamʿ until he reached Minā, then something happened to him, so he did not stone the Jamrah until the sun had set.
He عليه السلام said: “He should stone when morning comes, twice: one of them early in the morning, and it is for yesterday, and the other at the decline of the sun.”

key_terms.أَفَاضَ: departed and proceeded onward during the rites of hajj
key_terms.الْجَمْرَةَ: the Jamrah, the stoning site in the hajj rites
key_terms.زَوَالِ الشَّمْسِ: the sun’s decline from midday, i.e. noon time
key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, the place where the pelting rites are performed

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if he misses stoning the Jamrah at Minā until after sunset?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who missed the stoning of the Jamrah at Minā before sunset due to some intervening circumstance. He is to make it up the next morning with one stoning for the missed day and another at zawāl for the present day.
